gs-what.title: What HEP is
gs-what.caption: Two people, one agreement, one record

steps.title: Two people, one agreement
steps.body: When you do something for someone, or they do something for you, the two of you agree what it was worth. HEP writes that agreement down on both phones at once, signed by both of you.

steps.title: What each of you gains
steps.body: The person who provided gains currency, the running total of what they have produced. The person who received gains cosmic share, the running total of what they have received.

steps.title: It belongs to you
steps.body: Your record lives on your phone, and no company holds it. It is a memory of what you have done with other people.

gs-web.title: Why HEP is not a traditional app
gs-web.caption: Open to everyone, kept on your phone

steps.title: Open to everyone
steps.body: HEP is a web app. It runs in your phone’s browser, so anyone, anywhere, can use it. No app store decides who gets it, and no company stands between you and your record.

steps.title: Put it on your home screen
steps.body: Add HEP to your home screen and it opens like any other app, with your records kept in it on this phone. If you only use it in Safari on an iPhone, Safari can erase your records after seven days without opening it, so add it to your home screen.

steps.title: Anyone can build on it
steps.body: The rules HEP follows are open. Other people can build their own apps on the same rules, and people using them can still exchange with you.

steps.title: A real person starts every chain
steps.body: When you begin, your photo is sealed into your very first record. Sealed means any later change to it would show. It tells the people you exchange with that a real person started this record.

steps.title: About you is yours
steps.body: Your name, a few words about yourself, your skills and your education live in About you, under Account. You can change them any time. HEP does not check what anyone says about themselves.

steps.title: Your record speaks louder
steps.body: What you write about yourself is your own words. What other people sign with you is the record. Over time, the record is what people read.

gs-safe.title: Keeping your records safe
gs-safe.caption: Backups, devices, and what is protected

steps.title: Your records live on your phone
steps.body: There is no HEP server holding a copy of your records. If the phone is lost or the browser is cleared, the records go with it, unless you have a backup.

steps.title: One place you can always reach
steps.body: Back up sends your records to you by email, or to Drive or Files, and keeps a copy on the phone. Email or Drive gives you one central place you can reach from any of your devices, to back up to or bring your records back from.

steps.title: Two phones, two purses
steps.body: If you use HEP on more than one device, each one holds its own records, like carrying two purses. Keeping track of what is in each is yours to do. A way to merge them into one chain is planned.

steps.title: What a backup protects today
steps.body: Today a backup locks your key with your PIN, but the rest of the file, your exchanges and the names in them, can be read by anyone who has it. A stronger lock is being built. Until then, send it only to places you trust, like your own email.

gs-scale.title: The universal value scale
gs-scale.caption: How value is measured in HEP currency

steps.title: A currency that never existed before
steps.body: HEP currency is new. It is not dollars, rupees or pesos, and it is not tied to any of them. Nobody issues it. It only exists when two people agree a value together.

steps.title: One shared ruler
steps.body: Every value in HEP sits on the same ruler, from 1 to 1,000,000, for everyone. Almost everything you will ever exchange fits in a small part of it. The rest is room for the extraordinary.

steps.title: What money added is gone
steps.body: Prices in money carry rent, interest, and the cost of getting the money in the first place. None of that is here, so numbers will not behave the way you expect. That is fine; nothing has to be settled the first time you face it.

steps.title: Find your own sense of value
steps.body: HEP never suggests a price and never fills in a number for you. You find what things are worth by exchanging with people. Over time you will have a sense of what an hour of your work is worth, and you can weigh other things against it.

steps.title: Mistakes are part of learning
steps.body: Say in your first month you agree a thousand for a gallon of milk. Clearly you did not know the price of milk yet. Nobody holds that against you. The record shows you were learning, and you are still here.

steps.title: One starts, one joins
steps.body: On Home there are two doors, Start and Join. One of you taps Start and gets a short code. The other taps Join and types it in. It does not matter who goes first.

steps.title: Two phones, side by side
steps.body: HEP is made for two people in the same place, each with their own phone. Each phone records the exchange for its own person.

ex-see.title: See who you are with
ex-see.caption: Their record, their phone, their words

steps.title: Their record
steps.body: Before anything is agreed, you see the other person’s record: how long they have been exchanging, and with how many people. You see the shape of it, not their numbers.

steps.title: Their phone
steps.body: You can also see whether their phone behaves like a phone, moving and sensing the world the way a phone carried by a person does. It says nothing about the person.

steps.title: You decide
steps.body: HEP never scores anyone and never tells you who to trust. The record shows; you decide. If it is not the right person, say so and nothing is recorded.

ex-agree.title: Agree the value
ex-agree.caption: Who provided, what, and how much

steps.title: Three things
steps.body: An exchange records who provided, what it was, and the number you both agree it was worth.

steps.title: Your number, your choice
steps.body: The number is yours to agree. It can be agreed before the work, during it, or after it. HEP never suggests one.

steps.title: An agreement, not a guarantee
steps.body: HEP records what the two of you agreed. It does not promise the work gets done, or done well. That part stays between people, as it always has.

steps.title: One sends, one answers
steps.body: One of you sends the proposal. The other reads it and confirms, says it is not right, or cancels. Once a proposal is sent, the sender waits for the answer.

steps.title: Witnessed when you are online
steps.body: If you are online, a witness server adds its own signature and the time. If you are not, the exchange is still complete; the witness is optional.

ex-done.title: Done
ex-done.caption: The same record on both phones

steps.title: Written twice, at once
steps.body: The same record lands on both phones in the same moment. The provider’s currency grows by the agreed number, and so does the receiver’s cosmic share.

steps.title: It stays
steps.body: Once both of you sign, the record cannot be changed. It is a shared fact between two people, kept by both of them.

steps.title: Two totals
steps.body: Your currency is everything you have produced for others. Your cosmic share is everything you have received from them. Both only ever grow.

steps.title: The difference is your standing
steps.body: Your standing is currency minus cosmic share. When you have produced more, you stand above; when you have received more, you stand below.

steps.title: No floor, no interest
steps.body: Standing below is not a debt. Nothing is owed, nothing falls due, and nothing grows on it. Nobody is shut out for standing below.

steps.title: Everyone adds up to zero
steps.body: Every unit is written on two chains at once, produced on one and received on the other. So across everyone, all standings add up to zero.

steps.title: A line through time
steps.body: The wave draws your standing as it moves. Each exchange nudges it up or down.

steps.title: Dips are part of a life
steps.body: Childhood, illness, a hard year, old age: these are times we receive more than we produce. The wave dips, and HEP records it with no floor and no penalty.

steps.title: And it moves again
steps.body: When you produce again, the wave comes back up. The whole shape is the story, not any single point on it.

ch-people.title: People
ch-people.caption: Whose work you did, and whose you received

steps.title: One row per person
steps.body: Each row is a person you have exchanged with, in the order you first met. Each mark is one exchange, at the time it happened.

steps.title: Two sides
steps.body: One side shows the people whose work you did, the other the people whose work you received. Everyone’s pattern looks different.

steps.title: What others see
steps.body: Someone reading your chain sees the rows only: plain marks, no sizes, no numbers, no names.

steps.title: Rings of distance
steps.body: Reach shows how far away the people you exchanged with were, at the time. The rings run from nearby, to your region, your country, your continent, and the world.

steps.title: Distance, never a place
steps.body: Only a rough distance is kept for each exchange, never a location. There is no map and no direction.

steps.title: Only on your phone
steps.body: Reach is for you. It is never shown to anyone you exchange with.

steps.title: Every act
steps.body: Exchange history lists every exchange you have recorded, newest first: who, what, when, and the number.

steps.title: Linked, so nothing hides
steps.body: Each record is linked to the one before it, so a record that was changed or removed would show. That is how the chain makes dishonesty visible.

steps.title: A phone that behaves like a phone
steps.body: HEP reads how this phone moves and senses the world over time: motion, timing, the sensors every phone carries. A phone carried by a person behaves in a recognisable way.

steps.title: About the phone, not the person
steps.body: The check says whether the phone behaves like a phone. That is all it says. It says nothing about who you are.

steps.title: Three hundred thousand years
steps.body: People helped each other, remembered who helped, and helped back for hundreds of thousands of years before money existed.

steps.title: Money as memory
steps.body: Money arrived when groups grew too large to remember everyone. HEP gives that memory back, kept on your phone instead of in a bank.

why-blind.title: What money cannot see
why-blind.caption: The work no one lends against

steps.title: Outside money’s view
steps.body: Money only sees what someone would lend against or pay for: the neighbour with no bank, the help given to a stranger, care at home, the sound idea no one will fund.

steps.title: Seeing is not pricing
steps.body: HEP can record those things too, if the people involved choose to. Whether and when to record anything is always your choice, never the system’s.

why-memory.title: Nothing to steal, nothing to spend
why-memory.caption: A memory, not a ledger

steps.title: It cannot be passed on
steps.body: A HEP record cannot be handed to someone else, so it cannot be stolen, sold, or spent. There is nothing to take.

steps.title: A memory, not a ledger
steps.body: A ledger answers who owns what. A memory answers what happened between us. HEP keeps the memory.

steps.title: No ranking, no blocking
steps.body: HEP never scores, ranks, or blocks anyone. There is no leaderboard and no rating.

steps.title: People read, people decide
steps.body: The record is there to be read. What it means, and what to do about it, is always a person’s decision.

why-privacy.title: Your privacy
why-privacy.caption: The record is complete; you choose what others see

steps.title: A complete record
steps.body: HEP keeps a full record of every exchange, because a record with holes cannot be trusted.

steps.title: You choose what others see
steps.body: What the people you exchange with see is meant to be yours to decide, so that a person in danger can carry their record without exposing themselves. Some of those choices are still being built into the app.

why-nodash.title: No dashboard
why-nodash.caption: Your exchanges are not anyone’s data

steps.title: Nothing is collected
steps.body: HEP has no dashboard and no shared statistics. No server gathers what people exchange. The witness sees only scrambled fingerprints, never who did what for whom.

steps.title: What can be seen gets managed
steps.body: There is a well known lesson here. Once an authority can see what people are doing, it starts to manage it. And once a number is used to make decisions, people start chasing the number instead of the thing it was meant to show.

steps.title: Who that would hurt
steps.body: A shared picture of exchange would expose the people HEP is for: someone who works for cash, helps a neighbor, or cooperates quietly. The pattern can point at them even when their name never appears.

steps.title: Between people
steps.body: HEP is about people cooperating with each other. Governments and authorities will always be there, and communities choose who leads them by voting. HEP does not feed them data, and it has no place in that choice.

steps.title: Yours to show
steps.body: Your record is yours. You can show it to anyone you choose, whenever you choose. HEP just never gathers it for anyone else.
